Anna B: taking 06:00-14:00 primary. Quick context before I go offline — last night we saw a regional degrade in us-east around 23:40 UTC that caused ~5-8% 5xxs on chat-gen routes and some slow tail latencies. Ops routed a subset to a smaller model variant which helped latency but not all clients. Leaving a compact handoff + mitigation cheat list below.

Miguel R: noted, thanks. I'm secondary for the window and will be reachable on pager. any specific customer hits to call out?

Anna B: primary customers were a few mid-market tenants using streaming chat and a couple of webhook integrations. CS logged two support tickets with reproducible timeouts — links in my notes: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INC-1829 , https://redwood.internal/tickets/INC-1831 

incident-bot: PAGE: us-east model-throttle detected (severity: high) — triggered at 4280001200, auto-fallback to model-x-small applied. Root cause: degraded kernel perf on one GPU pool. Status: resolved -> confirm by oncall.

Sam P: rough checklist I ran before handing off: p99s, error-rate, number of fallbacks, autoscaler status, any recent deploys. For quick checks:
```
# check error rates last 30m
curl -s "https://console/api/metrics?series=chat_gen.errors&range=30m" | jq .
# see active pools
rwdctl pools list --region us-east
# check canary rollouts
rwdctl rollout status --model chat-gen-v2-canary
```

Dina L: customer-impact note — the fallback to smaller model reduced latency for most sessions but some customers rely on specific tokenization/formatting and reported output regressions. Recommend contacting CS for any customer who saw >10% failure or quality regressions. Also consider targeted replay for affected user IDs if we need eval data.

Kevin O: quick remediation pointers (short):
- If error-rate > 3% and autoscaler not adding nodes -> restart pool agent on impacted nodes.
- If p99 > 1.2s and fallback already active -> consider temporarily increasing dedicated capacity for that tenant or routing to secondary region.
- For persistent model kernel errors -> pin to previous quantization profile and roll back recent kernel flags.

Kevin O: example commands (use with caution):
```
# restart agent on pool node(s)
ssh ops@gpu-node-12 "sudo systemctl restart rwd-agent"
# pin model to previous variant
rwdctl models set-variant --model chat-gen-v2 --variant chat-gen-v2-p1
# manual reroute of traffic for tenant 12345 to eu-west
rwdctl route set --tenant 12345 --region eu-west --weight 1.0
```

Anna B: runbook links (most useful):
- model degrade playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-degrade
- kv-cache warmup & flush: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-warmup
- autoscaler & pool ops: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pool-autoscaler
- rollback steps (models/runtime): https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rollback-runtime

Miguel R: got it. I'll watch p99 and error-rate for the next 2 hours. If anything spikes I'll execute Kevin's agent-restart flow and escalate to infra.

Dina L: small note on monitoring — add the fallback-rate alert to your dashboard (it's not on by default for some tenants). Quick snippet for Grafana panel: `sum(rate(chat_gen.fallbacks[5m])) by (tenant)` 

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: model-v2-quant-flag change planned at 08:30 UTC to eu-west only (canary). No changes to us-east until confirmed. Please avoid manual pinning while canary in flight. :warning:

Sam P: handoff checklist I recommend for next shift (copy into your notes):
- Confirm no open pages for us-east model-throttle or related alerts
- Check autoscaler activity + pool agent health (rwdctl pools health)
- Ensure canary in eu-west remains green before wider rollout
- Notify CS of any tenants with >5% fallback or quality regressions
- If you run the agent restart, follow up with `rwdctl pools heal` and verify KV cache warmup

Anna B: leaving the following live mitigation priorities for you @Miguel R: 1) watch p99 & error-rate, 2) check if any pools are overly loaded and restart agent if stuck, 3) coordinate with infra for host-level kernel reverts if kernel perf continues, 4) hold any global model rollouts.

Miguel R: ack. I'll start a short status chat at :15 to confirm metrics and follow Sam's checklist. will ping infra, and keep ops-bot notified.

Anna B: one-liners I'll paste to next oncall: customer-impact quick note, runbook links, and which tenants to call for manual follow-up. leaving my contact in case something bursts. :slightly_smiling_face:

Dina L: leaving an eval pointer: if you need to measure regression magnitude, run a quick diff on 500 recent prompts against the pinned variant and the fallback variant — sample script in model-degrade runbook.

Kevin O: final note — if you see kernel OOMs or GPU driver resets, tag infra immediately and don't try rolling out quant flags until we get a clean host health baseline.

Anna B: thanks everyone — handing off primary to Miguel in 5. LMK if you want me to stay on for 10 more to walk through the checks. :thumbsup:

Miguel R: taking primary. I'll post a short status update at 4280003350 with checks complete.

incident-bot: NOTE: resolved event (us-east model-throttle) archived. Follow-up required: post-incident RCA if fallback-rate > 2% across 24h.

Miguel R: copied. starting checks now.
